misconceptions.description: Assuming biomimetic architecture is mainly about copying outer form
misconceptions.trigger: learner focuses on mound appearance without discussing airflow and thermal behavior
misconceptions.feedback: The valuable principle is the coupled system of airflow, vent layout, thermal mass, and environmental response, not just the outer silhouette.

misconceptions.description: Thinking passive systems do not require deliberate engineering
misconceptions.trigger: learner treats passive cooling as uncontrolled natural ventilation
misconceptions.feedback: Passive does not mean accidental. Successful passive cooling depends on carefully designed geometry, materials, and environmental fit.

misconceptions.description: Assuming thermal mass is universally beneficial in every climate and use case
misconceptions.trigger: learner recommends thermal mass without considering local conditions or cycling
misconceptions.feedback: Thermal mass helps only when the timing of heat storage and release matches the climate and operating pattern. Context matters.
